scope: entire repository (siril_mcp.py, 264 lines, single commit 94ab153); angles 3 and 4 skipped (no history), test review and coverage skipped (no tests / no coverage tool at the time)

findings.description: `siril_preview` calls `session.run` directly and skips `_run`'s catch-`SirilError` → `session.stop()` reset. After a mid-preview timeout the session stays alive with the command still running, the `finally` sends `load snap` into it, and the restore error replaces the original one. The lock/run/raise handling is hand-copied from `_run` and has already diverged with nothing to catch it (this is what lifts it to High). angles [2,5,6,7,8,9]; also I1,I2,V1-V3.

The terminal `status: success|error <cmd>` line's command echo is never compared to the issued command, so a late status from an earlier command is returned as the next command's result. Silent wrong data with a success status. Reproduced: after a timed-out `stat`, `load "nonexistent"` returned `(True, <stat output>)`. Today reachable via F03 and F09. angles [5,9]; also I1,I2,V1-V3.
findings.disposition_reason: fixed: status lines are matched to the command verb. Residual: a stale status for the SAME verb as the next command cannot be told apart (documented in README; a timeout resets the session so it is unlikely).

findings.description: Input validation (empty command, newline/CR in a command or any file/path argument) raises `SirilError`, which `_run` treats as fatal: `session.stop()` and "(session reset)". One bad tool argument destroys the loaded/processed image though nothing was sent to Siril. Reproduced (`siril_command "stat\nstat"`). angles [2,5]; also I2,V3.

Multi-line Siril log messages lose every line after the first (continuation lines have no `log: ` prefix and fall into the silent "other kinds" branch, no counter). `siril_help()` returned 203 of 240 lines; `siril_help("stack")` loses its syntax lines (also register, platesolve, seqapplyreg, makepsf, rgbcomp, stackall, update_key); tool reports success. A continuation line beginning `status: success` would be read as a terminal marker. Bare `log:` and unknown prefixes are dropped too. Violates the Data-Capture rule (dropped with no reason or counter). angles [1,2,5,9]; also V1-V3.

Out FIFO opened `O_RDWR`, so the process is its own writer and the reader never sees EOF; the "Siril process exited" branch and `None` sentinel are dead code. A Siril crash/kill/`exit` waits the full timeout (default 300s) and is reported as "timed out". Verified. angles [1,2,5,7,8,9]; also I1,I2,V1-V3.

`exit`, `quit` and script (`@script.ssf`) invocations never emit a terminal status: the call hangs to timeout then resets the session. Binary also contains `status: exit`/`status: busy`; an unknown status word is treated as non-terminal and hangs. README documents the protocol as complete. Verified. angles [1,5]; also I1,I2,V2,V3.

`timeout_s` is unvalidated: negative → `ValueError` after the command was written (no reset, output mis-paired with the next call, the F04 path); 0 → always times out and resets; `inf` → `OverflowError`. Verified for -1 and 0. angles [1,2]; also I1,I2.
Per-tool hardcoded timeouts (30/60/120s) ignore `SIRIL_MCP_TIMEOUT`, which the README presents as the per-command default; an overrun triggers the destructive reset. 6 sites. angles [5].

Siril's python-venv bootstrap `log:` lines arrive after `ready` and after the first command's terminal status, contaminating whichever command is in flight; the pre-command drain only removes already-queued lines. Intermittent. angles [1]; also I1,I2.
findings.disposition_reason: mitigated: output before the command's own 'starting' marker is dropped. Residual: bootstrap logs arriving between a command's starting and terminal lines can still appear in its output (documented).

findings.description: `siril_set_directory` validates against the server's cwd but Siril resolves `cd` against its own cwd; `session.workdir` is set before the `cd` succeeds and outside the lock; a raw `siril_command("cd ...")` never updates it, so a reset silently reverts the directory; Siril started with a missing `-d` silently runs with cwd `(null)`. angles [1,2,5,9]; also I1,I2,V1.

Siril stdout/stderr go to DEVNULL, exit code/signal never read, pre-`ready` lines discarded, reader swallows OSError. Every startup failure or crash shows only "timed out"/"Siril process exited". angles [9]; also V1-V3.

`siril_preview` docstring says the stretch applies to "a temporary copy"; it actually mutates the live image then restores from a temp FITS snapshot. Afterwards Siril's current filename points at the deleted temp `snap.fit`; undo history and boxselect are lost. Pixel data/bit depth verified preserved at 16/32-bit. angles [1,5,9]; also I1,I2.
findings.disposition_reason: fixed: docstring is honest, nothing is snapshotted when nothing mutates, restore is skipped after a reset. Side effects of save/load restore (current-file name, undo history, selection) remain and are documented.

findings.description: Cleanup only in `finally`: if the Python process dies (SIGKILL/SIGTERM) an orphan `siril-cli` keeps running and the pipe dir is left behind. No atexit/signal handler. A leftover pipe dir was found on disk during this review. angles [1,2].

Default `max_dim=0` returns a full-resolution JPEG, which for tens-of-megapixel frames may exceed MCP/API image limits (untested at scale). The snapshot/reload also runs when nothing mutates the image (`autostretch=False`, `max_dim=0`), and the stretch runs before the shrink. angles [1,8].
findings.disposition_reason: fixed: default max_dim 2048, snapshot skipped when nothing mutates. 'stretch before shrink' kept deliberately (more faithful). resample also enlarges small images (documented).

findings.description: Siril flags (`-p -r -w -d`), `ready`, `exit`, prefixes, `savejpg` appending `.jpg`, `resample -maxdim=` are assumed with no version gate or smoke check ("observed on 1.4.5" but never checked). mcp `>=1.2` lower bound never exercised (only 1.30 tested). angles [9]; also I1,I2,V3.

The save-format→command map in `siril_save` is hand-typed; `siril_preview` re-hardcodes `save`/`savejpg … 90` and `.jpg` instead of consuming it; preview trusts `status: success` then does a raw `read_bytes()`. Not yet diverged. angles [6]; also I1,V2.
No tests for the only source file (`missing_test_sweep.py`); modified today; README admits it. Most defects above are what a fake-pipe-peer test would pin. mechanical sweep.
findings.disposition_reason: fixed: 116-test suite against a fake Siril plus pytest-cov (96% line+branch, 90% floor) added in commit d30d892.

findings.description: `out_fd` never closed; each `start()` leaks 1 fd, 1 blocked daemon thread, 1 queue. Low on exposure: `start()` runs only on reset/crash restart, ~250 restarts to hit the macOS fd limit; re-rate if resets become frequent. angles [1,2,6,7,8,9].
Timeout is per received line, not per command; README says "per-command". Not reproduced. angles [1,2,5,9]; also V3.
findings.disposition_reason: fixed by making the documented contract match the behaviour: the timeout is an idle timeout (any output restarts it), so a long stack that keeps reporting is not cut off. Code unchanged by design; README, docstrings and a test say so.

findings.description: Paths interpolated as `"{x}"` with no escaping at 6 sites; Siril has no escape for `"`; names with `"` are saved mangled or inject an extra argument. Newlines rejected; `siril_command` already allows arbitrary Siril commands. Low on exposure (names containing `"` are rare). angles [2,5,6,9]; also I1,I2.

Missing/non-executable `SIRIL_BIN` raises a raw `FileNotFoundError` that `_run` does not catch; `mkdtemp` dir leaks until the next `stop()`; silent fallback to `/opt/homebrew/bin/siril-cli`. One start path. angles [2,9]; also I1,V2,V3.
`os.write` return value unchecked (Unchecked-Result rule). One helper, 2 call sites. Low on exposure. angles [2,5]; also V1-V3.
"no image loaded" inferred from process liveness; mislabels a dead/never-started process. 1 site. angles [7,9]; also V1-V3.
`status: error` with no `log:` line gives an empty failure reason ("Siril command failed: <cmd>\n"). angles [1]; also I2,V2.
`proc.kill()` not followed by `wait()` (zombie); the 5s wait holds `session.lock`. Rare path, 1 site. angles [2,8,9].
Unbounded queue / log list / line buffer (no truncation flag) and O(n²) `buf.split(b"\n",1)`. Not measured; largest observed output ~240 lines. Low on exposure. angles [8]; also V3.
findings.disposition_reason: fixed: returned text capped with a marker, O(n) line splitting, over-long lines split and flagged. The idle queue is still unbounded (Siril is silent when idle apart from bootstrap logs; accepted).

findings.description: Synchronous `is_dir()` on the event loop; queued calls park executor threads on `session.lock`. Single user, 1 stat call. angles [8].
`_reader` hand-rolls line splitting where `os.fdopen(fd,"rb").readline()` would do; `decode("utf-8","replace")` silently substitutes. Single copy, 1 site. angles [6]; also V1-V3.
findings.disposition_reason: fixed: O(n) splitting; invalid UTF-8 replacement kept and documented. os.fdopen(...).readline() not adopted because the reader needs select() to be stoppable.

findings.description: Minor simplification: one-element `for fd in (self.in_fd,)`, duplicated priming call, inline drain loop, `assert` that vanishes under `-O`, status vocabulary split across `TERMINAL_STATUSES` and an inline `"starting"`, unused `workdir` param, thin wrapper tools. angles [7].
findings.disposition_reason: fixed except the thin wrapper tools (siril_help/load/save/stats), which are the intended tool surface and are kept.

findings.description: Log truncation is not monotonic: a short line after a dropped over-long one is still appended, leaving a gap while the marker claims everything after was dropped.
Shutdown after stdin EOF waits for the in-flight command (asyncio.run joins the executor thread before mcp.run returns), so cleanup runs late or an orphaned Siril is left.
findings.disposition_reason: fixed: a cancelled tool call aborts Siril. Depends on mcp>=1.27, which cancels in-flight calls on disconnect; floor raised accordingly.

_reap_stale_dirs raises on odd directory names (non-ASCII digits, out-of-range numbers), failing every session start until the dir is removed. Contrived trigger.
resample -maxdim=N also enlarges images smaller than N, so the default preview size can make small images bigger.

README says every tool uses the default timeout, but siril_command takes timeout_s.

findings.disposition_reason: replaced by a counting-lock test asserting at most one thread reaches session.lock.

scope: delta c4cb687..6461c3e: log summarising (siril_mcp.py, tests/fake_siril.py, tests/test_logs.py, README.md)

findings.description: `condense_log` fills the "rare lines" section from the head of the log and `break`s at the first line that exceeds the budget, so the **last** rare lines are dropped: Siril's terminal `Error:` line, closing totals, and this server's own end-of-log markers (`[output truncated…]`, `[ignored N stale status line(s)…]`, `[unrecognised terminal status…]`, which travel as plain text and cannot be told from Siril output). `run_checked` (594-596) puts this summary into the `RuntimeError`, so a failed command can show the model no failure reason; only "N more such line(s) omitted" appears. README.md:42 and the docstring (191-194) claim warnings, errors and closing totals survive. Reproduced by angles 1, 3, 9 and the test audit (e.g. 1500 distinct lines + final `Error: the real failure` → error absent); exposed whenever a >20,000-char log has lines that differ in letters (filenames, ids), which `_shape` never collapses. High rather than Critical: the omission is announced, the saved-log path is in the header, and a 400-frame `calibrate` log (repetitive) summarises fine.

the "full log" is the already-processed output of `run()`: capped at `MAX_LOG_CHARS` (1,000,000) with a truncation marker, `progress:` and pre-`starting` lines dropped, notices prepended, stale/truncation markers appended. "Complete and unaltered" (README.md:45), the header's "full log saved" and its line/character counts are therefore false whenever the cap fires, and the README says "unaltered" about text that is relative to what `run()` returned. Neither layer knows about the other and nothing ties them together. Only logs over 1M chars lose content.

the prune `sorted(LOG_DIR.glob("*.log"))[:-MAX_LOG_FILES]` is not tied to the names `_save_full_log` writes. With `SIRIL_MCP_LOG_DIR` pointing at a shared directory, unrelated `*.log` files are counted and deleted, and foreign names that sort after the digit-prefixed ones make the server's own logs the oldest. Reproduced: with 55-60 foreign `app*.log` files (or `MAX_LOG_FILES=1`) the log just written was pruned while the header still said "full log saved to <path>" and the comment "the log just written is already safe" was false. A clock stepping backwards has the same effect. `_reap_stale_dirs` has an ownership guard; this has none, and the test uses an empty dedicated directory. The default directory is dedicated, so exposure is the env override only.

`_shape` masks digits, so repeated per-item errors that differ only in frame/file number (e.g. 30× `Error: could not open frame_NNNNN.fit`) collapse to `Nx first-example` once more than 3; which items failed is only in the saved file, and a failed command's error text can lose it. Counted, not silent, but README.md:42 "warnings, errors … survive" overstates it; the "numbers are masked" heading is the only hint. Pass 3 suggests a distinct-variant count per shape. Untested.
findings.disposition_reason: fixed in part: the heading and README now say lines differing only in numbers are grouped and only the first is shown; the grouping itself is kept (counted, and the saved log has every line)

findings.description: the `- 300` reserve for headings/omission notes is an unverified guess (fixed text sums to ~260, margin ~40) and nothing asserts `len(out) <= RETURN_LOG_CHARS` after assembly. The bound holds at defaults (19,515-19,846 of 20,000 in worst-case runs) but with small limits the output exceeds the limit (3,518 chars at limits 2000/1000/400) and can exceed the original log; fixed overhead is ~3,000 chars (15 kinds × (160 + marker)), which is the real reason for the documented "soft below a few thousand" floor. `160`/`600`/`+ 3` are unnamed literals. angles [2,5,7,9]; see #50.

the 20,000 default (and "at most 3", "newest 50") is hand-typed in the code, the README and the `siril_command` docstring that the client model reads; the docstring is fixed text, so it states the wrong threshold whenever `SIRIL_MCP_LOG_LIMIT` is set. The other tools that go through `run_checked` (`siril_help`, `siril_load`, `siril_save`, `siril_stats`) say nothing about summarising. The tests import the constants, so nothing checks the docs.

`condense_log` runs after Siril has already completed the command, outside the `try/except SirilError`; any unexpected non-`OSError` exception inside it would discard a good result or replace the real failure reason with a traceback (same shape as earlier finding d1bf#03). No trigger known today (135 tests, 96% coverage). It also does file I/O inside `session.lock` (measured ~1 ms write, ~16 ms total at the 1M cap: not a problem).

catalogue-style output of unique lines would be head-truncated by #01 if it exceeded the limit; real `help` is 11,167 chars vs 20,000 (~1.8× headroom), so agreement is held only by headroom; with a lowered `SIRIL_MCP_LOG_LIMIT` or a bigger future Siril, `siril_help` is silently summarised head-first and its docstring does not say so. Exposure today: 0 (one call site, default fine). Interface phase rated this Medium; kept at the higher rating.

reuse: the env-parsing idiom was copied next to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` rather than shared, and the copies have already diverged (the timeout is validated per call by `_validate_timeout`; the log limit is not), which is what produced #12. Three hand-formatted bracket markers ("[line cut…]", "[line split…]", "[output truncated…]") with differing wording and no common formatter. Medium by the Reuse floor.

the whole prune loop is under one `except OSError: pass`: the first failing `unlink` (permission, or `FileNotFoundError` from a second server pruning the same directory) aborts pruning the rest, with no counter or notice, so "newest 50 are kept" can silently stop holding.

a write failure after `mkstemp` (disk full) returns `(None, reason)` but leaves a partial or empty `.log` that takes a slot in the 50-file window; an `os.fdopen` failure would leak the fd. The header correctly says "could NOT be saved"; the test covers only `mkdir` failure. Exposure: disk-full only.

`SIRIL_MCP_LOG_LIMIT` unvalidated: a non-integer (`20k`, empty) raises `ValueError` at import (loud, bare traceback); 0 or a negative value summarises every non-empty log and gives a negative budget so no rare lines are shown. `SIRIL_MCP_LOG_DIR` has no `expanduser` (`~/x` creates a literal `~` directory under the server's cwd — verified), a relative value gives a cwd-dependent header path, `Path.home()` is evaluated at import, and unset-vs-empty is handled differently for the two variables. README documents no constraints. Exposure: env vars unset by default, one user.

"rare" and "frequent" are the same predicate against `RARE_LINE_MAX` written at two sites in opposite directions; a one-sided edit would be caught by the 3/4 boundary test; only the README's hard-coded "3" is unenforced.
findings.disposition_reason: wontfix: both sites are pinned by the 3/4 boundary test, which also asserts a four-times line is not listed verbatim; README's '3' is documentation

findings.description: "`log:` text is passed back to the model unparsed" and "Returned text is capped at 1,000,000 characters" are stale for logs over the limit (summarised with numbers masked; effective cap ~20,000). Maintainer-facing.

on `SirilError` (timeout, process death) the partial log accumulated in `_collect` is discarded (only the 2,000-byte console tail is in the error), so the "saved to a file" promise does not extend to the case where a long-running convert/register log would help diagnose. Feature gap, not a regression.
findings.disposition_reason: deferred: feature gap (no saved log on timeout or process death); the error carries Siril's console tail. Low, no known occurrence

findings.description: `command.split(None, 1)[0]` raises `IndexError` for an empty command if `condense_log`/`_save_full_log` are called directly (unreachable via `run_checked`, which validates first); the verb-extraction idiom is duplicated at 508; the 30-character cap and the `"cmd"` fallback are untested.

the file name carries two timestamps of the same instant (`time_ns` + `strftime`) so a lexical sort matches time order; "newest" is encoded in a filename string rather than `st_mtime` or a counter (and is the mechanism behind #03).

findings.description: every `_cut` mutant survives: `<=`→`<`, default 600→599/601, slice `[:limit+1]`, example limit 160→159/161, and removing the 160 cap entirely. The only test asserts the substring "…[line cut, 5000 characters]" on one 5000-char line. Removing the 160 cap leaves the "Repeated lines" section unbounded, so the bounded-summary guarantee is untested for repeated examples.
`used + len(item) + 3 > budget` → `>=`, budget+1 and dropping the `+3` all survive; the only budget test asserts `len(shown) > 50` (actual ~113) and `len(out) <= LIMIT`.

the `- 300` reserve is unpinned: 300→299 and 300→301 survive; tests only assert `len(out) <= LIMIT` (and `< LIMIT + 200` for the failure message), so a reserve that is too small goes unnoticed until real headings plus notes (~260 fixed chars) overflow. Suggested pin: `LIMIT-400 < len(out) <= LIMIT`. (See #05.)

`counts[sh] <= RARE_LINE_MAX` → `<= RARE_LINE_MAX+1` survives: four-times lines would then appear both verbatim and in the repeated section; the test asserts only that "4x same x 1" is present, never that the line is absent from the verbatim list. Add `out.count("same x 1") == 1`.
a mutation to least-common-first listing (`most_common()[::-1]`) survives because tests/test_logs.py:107 gives all 20 kinds an equal count of 5; "the most repeated kinds are listed" is untested.

prune mutants survive: `glob("*.log")`→`glob("*")` (foreign files) and `except OSError: pass`→re-raise (a failing prune is untested). Real code swallows a failing prune correctly (probed); nothing guards it. Related: #03.

`if omitted:` / `if rare:` / `if repeated:` forced to `True` survive: nothing asserts the omission note or the section headings are absent when nothing was omitted or there are no rare lines (a false "0 more omitted" would break "never silent" in reverse).

no test for the terminal error line being the last rare line under budget pressure (probe: 400 distinct lines + final `Error: registration aborted…` → summary has no trace of the error; at a small limit even a first-line `Error: boom` vanishes because the budget goes negative). The fake's `spamfail` emits no error text at all, only status, while real failures log several rare cause lines ("Registration aborted.", "Preparing sequence processing failed."…) and a leading "Running command: <verb>" echo, so `test_a_failing_command_with_a_long_log…` checks only the prefix and the saved path. Add an `Error:` line as the final rare line to the fake and a variant with a very long failing log. Exposure today: needs >~19k chars of rare-shape lines; 0 known real cases. Related: #01.

the assertion `"/" not in path.name[len(str(path.parent)):]` is vacuous (`Path.name` never contains `/`; the `"werdverb" in path.name` assertion does the work). `MAX_LOG_FILES` is tested only with 5 saves against a limit of 3 (no exactly-N, N-1, N+1; no pin for `[:-MAX_LOG_FILES]` at 0), `MAX_SHAPES_SHOWN` only with 20 kinds (no 15 or 16), the order test pins one pair of lines, and the failing-write (not `mkdir`) and failing-prune paths are untested.

the comments say `convert` logs one or two lines per file; real siril-cli 1.4.5 `convert` on FITS logs only 3-4 lines in total (measured with 6, 12 and 400 files), while `calibrate` and `register` do log per file. The invented "Saving FITS" and 3-layer lines are unverified against a stored real long log (0 real captures are kept), real logs start with "Running command: <verb>" which the fake never emits, and real per-file lines can arrive out of order while the fake alternates strictly. No assertion depends on this; the `spam` line shapes match real `calibrate`. Whether convert of camera raw files (DNG) logs per file was not checked. also IF-11.
the verb cap `[:30]` (29, 31 and removed all survive) and the `or "cmd"` fallback are unpinned; only the sanitisation is. Exposure: 0 real commands have a verb over 30 characters or without letters.
cosmetic mutants survive (count width `>5`→`>4`, `split("\n")` vs `splitlines()`). `errors="replace"`→`"strict"` also survives but is equivalent (the reader already decodes with `replace`).
findings.disposition_reason: wontfix: cosmetic or equivalent mutants

findings.description: loose bounds: `len(msg) < LIMIT + 200` has 200 characters of slack that hides a reserve bug (see #50), and `len(shown) > 50` is checked against ~113 actual.

the fake's `distinct` shapes are all lowercase words; real logs carry varying floats and exponents (`e-05` vs `e+05` give different shapes `Ne-N` / `Ne+N`); the regex is unit-tested for `6.698e-05` but not this.
